instructions: Laplace-marginal HMC requires a latent Gaussian layer that can be analytically marginalized. MVN_10 is a direct Gaussian model with no hierarchical structure, so Laplace marginalization does not apply. This requires model parameterization work.
workflow:
Hard-exclusion category 7: Laplace-marginal for non-hierarchical / non-Gaussian models.

Laplace-marginal kernels (laplace_hmc, laplace_dhmc, laplace_mhmc, laplace_dmhmc) exclude all models without a latent Gaussian layer that can be analytically marginalized over the posterior. Concretely, they are unavailable for: mvn_10, ill_cond_50, logistic_syn, lotka_volterra, german_credit, gmm_25, banana, and horseshoe.

MVN_10 is a simple multivariate Gaussian model with no hierarchy — there are no latent parameters to marginalize. The Laplace-marginal sampler would need to define which parameters are latent and which are observed, a distinction that does not exist in the direct Gaussian formulation. Extending mvn_10 to support Laplace marginalization would require introducing an explicit latent Gaussian layer (e.g., a hierarchical prior on the covariance structure) that mvn_10 does not currently expose.

Models like eight_schools_ncp, radon, and irt_2pl are yellow (potentially feasible) because they have explicit latent Gaussian layers, but their PosteriorEntry schema does not yet record theta_init (the initialized latent position); this is Phase 7 scope.

See RECIPE_GENERATION.md § Hard Exclusions Category 7 (lines 597-599) for the full context.
